disciplinary_grounds.2234_b: Gross negligence — extreme departure from standard of care
disciplinary_grounds.2234_c: Repeated negligent acts — two or more separate departures from standard of care
disciplinary_grounds.2234_d: Incompetence — lack of knowledge or ability expected of licensees
disciplinary_grounds.2234_f: Fraudulent or corrupt acts — false billing, false diagnosis, unnecessary procedures
disciplinary_grounds.general: Any conduct inconsistent with professional standards (catch-all)

interpretive.rule: §2234(b) defines its own standard: 'extreme departure from the applicable standard of care, whether applied in the same or similar community.' Rule is from the statute text directly — not from judicial gloss.
interpretive.status: STATUTE_ANCHORED — case law applying §2234(b) exists in Medical Board OAH decisions and appellate review; specific citations pending verification

interpretive.rule: §2234(c) defines its own standard: two or more negligent acts or omissions, each a 'separate and distinct departure from the standard of care.' Rule is from the statute text directly — not from judicial gloss.
interpretive.status: STATUTE_ANCHORED — case law applying §2234(c) exists in Medical Board OAH decisions and appellate review; specific citations pending verification

board_complaint_grounds: §2234(b) gross negligence: performing surgery that was medically unnecessary = extreme departure from standard of care
§2234(c) repeated negligent acts: (1) inadequate pre-op workup, (2) unnecessary procedure, (3) false documentation
§2234(f) fraudulent acts: if surgery was performed for financial motives without medical indication; false billing for procedures not performed
evidence_needed: Billing records showing procedures billed vs. procedures documented
Any prior complaints against the surgeon in DCA BreEZe
Independent expert review of operative indication
spine_surgery_fraud.coordination: File Board complaint parallel to civil suit. Hrimnak escape removes MICRA caps for the civil case; §2234(f) fraudulent acts grounds the Board complaint in the same fraud theory.

board_complaint_grounds: §2234(b) gross negligence: if injection was administered to clearly incorrect anatomical location = extreme departure
§2234(c) repeated acts: if facility has documented pattern of SIRVA complaints from same vaccinators
evidence_needed: Vaccine administration record showing injection site
Post-injection treatment records documenting SIRVA diagnosis
Any other SIRVA complaints against same facility/provider

checklist_before_filing_board_complaint: Look up physician NPI at nppes.cms.hhs.gov
Gather medical records (request under H&S §123110 — free first copy for malpractice cases)
Note dates of all complained-of conduct (§2234(c) requires two separate acts)
File online at https://www.mbc.ca.gov/complaints/ with supporting records
